sections.title: Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text:
The legal issuer is Harshdeep Hortico Limited, CIN L26994MH2022PLC396421, BSE SME 544105, ISIN INE0OLZ01015. The annual-report cover's 544013 is a document typo, not a different issuer: the report body, other filings and official interoperable security master establish the identity. Incorporation was 30 December 2022; the promoter's Harshdeep Agro Products business was acquired as a going concern on 3 April 2023. Financial analysis is standalone because no subsidiary, associate or joint venture is disclosed at 31 March 2026. The accounts use Indian GAAP Accounting Standards, not assumed Ind AS. Units are ₹ crore unless specified. Information cutoff is 20 October 2026, Asia/Kolkata; sources retrieved on 21 October are restricted to pre-cutoff disclosures and historical observations.

The modeled holding interval is 19 October 2026 to 19 October 2031, five anniversary years; the equity hurdle is 15% nominal before investor tax, not an automatically selected WACC. The ₹96 reference is the latest retrieved secondary close dated 16 October, not a verified 19 October close. Equity value at 16,094,060 issued shares is ₹154.503 crore. The official 19 October master gives a 1,500-share lot. An illustrative ₹5 lakh budget buys three full lots, 4,500 shares costing ₹432,000; four lots cost ₹576,000 and exceed it. This is not a recommended allocation.

G1 is Conditional, G2/G3/G4 Hold — unresolved. Identity and transcription of dated primary totals have High confidence; underlying growth and cash-conversion direction Medium; attributable capital returns, current funding, financial reconciliation and executable liquidity Low. Overall investment confidence is Low because the weakest material input governs the conclusion. An unmodified audit and no reported repayment default are retained as counterevidence, not erased by the holds. [S1][S4][S5][M1][M2]

sections.title: Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text:
The canonical quality factors are GOV 5, MOAT 4, REV 8, DUR 6, CAP NS, CASH 4, BAL NS, EXEC 6 and EARN 5. IAS factors are R NS, D 3, P 5 and L NS. Each has two material facts, contrary evidence, confidence and citations in the embedded audit. No unknown factor is scored zero, five or a peer average.

BQS has exactly 4.24 known weighted contribution and 80% coverage. With 20% missing weight its mathematical bound is 4.44–6.24; the point is NS. GQS has 5.55 known contribution and 85% coverage; its bound is 5.70–7.05 and its point remains NS. IAS has 1.10 known contribution, 30% directly scored coverage and 70% missing inputs including BQS. Its direct mathematical bound is 1.80–8.10; propagating the tighter BQS interval gives 2.66–7.16. These are not confidence intervals or investable scores. BQS is reused only once at 25% in IAS; GQS means Growth Quality, not governance.

No governance/funding-failure cap is applied because no severe evidenced G1/G3 failure is established. CASH 4 reflects repeated weak conversion but does not trigger the explicit CASH ≤3 GQS cap. CAP is NS because its 19.51% book incremental-return proxy cannot be attributed to new investment. Moving MOAT and EXEC by one point together shifts the BQS bound by 0.28; moving DUR and EARN together shifts GQS by 0.35. These uncertainties do not fill evidence gaps. Every aggregate is excluded from numerical rankings and no matrix cell or compounder designation is forced. [S1–S5][S7][S8][M1][M2]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.text:
Harshdeep designs, manufactures and sells plastic indoor/outdoor, illuminated, decorative, rotationally moulded and FRP planters, plus garden accessories, outdoor furniture and shade nets. Cash is earned through distributor/dealer and retail channels, direct institutional projects and online intermediaries. A well-known installation is evidence that a purchase order exists, not evidence of a contractual annuity. Plastics, moulds, colour/design variety, production scheduling, freight and credit terms determine the economics. Revenue is recorded when the relevant sale conditions are met; customer advances and invoices have different cash timing.

The 2025 presentation describes three facilities around Mumbai/Bhiwandi, Pune and Delhi, approximately 160,000 square feet, ten distributors in four cities, five showrooms and a Bangalore warehouse. These are management descriptions, not independently certified capacity or current market share. The company expanded shade nets and announced decorative rotomoulded fountains in April 2026. The business is overwhelmingly domestic: FY26 foreign-currency earnings were ₹0.6438 crore versus ₹1.1370 crore in FY25, under 1% of FY26 operating revenue. Foreign-currency earnings are not silently equated with an audited geographic sales segment. No reportable segments are disclosed, and product/channel margins are ND.

Earlier risk disclosures identified Maharashtra as 41.99% of four-month July 2023 sales, top-ten customers 21.91% and top-ten raw-material suppliers 85.15%. Those dated concentrations are not treated as FY26 shares. Raw materials include polymer inputs susceptible to price volatility; short purchase arrangements can transmit cost and supply shocks. Inventory is a particularly important asset to realize rather than merely a balance-sheet indication of growth. [S1][S4][S6][S9]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.text:
The plausible mechanism is design breadth plus mould/tooling capability, distribution relationships and reliable project delivery. The evidence is a long predecessor operating history, multiple manufacturing technologies and actual airport purchase disclosures. The possible durability is lower procurement friction and a familiar supplier for varied project requirements. The failure mode is straightforward: plastic-planter designs can be copied, buyers can switch between organized and local vendors, polymer prices move and excess designs can sit unsold. No disclosed patent protection, recurring price premium, channel retention, share-gain series or new-product return proves a structural moat.

The comparison set is selected economically rather than to manufacture a peer P/E. Nilkamal is an adjacent, much larger moulded-furniture/material-handling and distribution benchmark. Supreme's furniture business explicitly uses injection, roto and blow moulding, showing that these technologies alone are not exclusive. Diplast's official catalogue includes plastic planters and outdoor products. Garden's Need is a direct private planter competitor with distributor/nursery/export routes. Their undated official product pages establish competitive alternatives only; advertised scale or leadership statements are not independently verified rankings or dated financial forecasts. Listed diversified groups are not pure-play planter valuation comparables, and private peers lack comparable public financials. A numeric peer median would therefore be misleading.

MOAT 4 recognizes useful but contestable commercial capabilities. Harshdeep's trademark transfer at nil consideration improves corporate ownership of the brand, but the filing says the registry application was made, not that final registry endorsement was retrieved. The company's first-of-its-kind fountain description and extended-product-life claims remain attributed management statements. [S1][S6][S8][S9][P1–P4]

sections.title: Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text:
The operating-business revenue series is ₹25.1905/34.8561/40.7670/48.2785/56.2676/68.7090 crore for FY21–FY26. The first three years are restated predecessor accounts; FY24–FY26 are the successor company. The five-year CAGR is 22.22%, using six observations, and FY23–FY26 three-year CAGR 19.01%. Ten-year CAGR is ND. Annual additions from FY22 are ₹9.6656,5.9109,7.5115,7.9891 and 12.4414 crore. No CAGR is calculated from the near-empty corporate FY23 revenue zero; that would confuse legal incorporation with the acquired business's operating history.

FY26 growth is 22.11%. H1FY26 operating sales ₹32.6419 crore compare with ₹24.8153 crore, up 31.54%. Derived H2FY26 ₹36.0671 crore compares with ₹31.4523 crore, up 14.67%. This slowing second half is relevant counterevidence, not a reason to annualize a quarter. No verified H1FY27 financial release was located by cutoff, so the latest comparable TTM remains FY26. H2 figures are annual-minus-H1 balancing values. Reported figures include a minor FY24 reclassification: original operating sales ₹48.2478 became ₹48.2785 in the later comparative, with offsetting other-income presentation.

Business continuity supports a five-year operating series, but scope/accounting differences remain explicit. Volume, realized price, channel mix and product additions are not separately quantified; nominal reported growth is not labeled constant-price organic volume growth. Dated airport orders are small relative to annual sales and tax-inclusive, so they are not added mechanically to forecast revenue. REV starts at 8 for the selected 22.22% five-year window, with net adjustment 0 and Medium-confidence ceiling 8. Three-year growth, current trajectory and absolute additions remain visible rather than choosing whichever window flatters the company. [S1–S5][S10][S11]

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text:
Demand access is plausible through nurseries, residential/office landscaping, hospitality and institutional facilities, plus adjacent shade-net and outdoor product uses. It is not justified by a broad agriculture or horticulture TAM. Management's November 2024 call said Bhiwandi utilization was 75%, planned 12,000 additional square feet at Pune and approximately 350,000 kg annual shade-net output. The 2025 presentation repeats 350,000 kg in its expansion narrative but shows 210,000 kg in a capacity graphic; it also mixes annual pieces with a Delhi three-month capacity. Those denominators are unreconciled, so no certified current group utilization or automatic growth headroom is invented.

The model includes a deliberately labeled bottom-up unit-equivalent check: annual sales divided by an assumed ₹250 blended unit value. That is a sensitivity, not reported unit volume, and kilograms of shade nets cannot simply be added to pieces of planters. At the base terminal annual run-rate of ₹149.64 crore, implied blended units are about 5.99 million; at bull ₹201.84 crore they are about 8.07 million. Product mix, actual realizations, moulding bottlenecks and qualification/fulfillment determine whether this arithmetic is feasible. Capex is separately funded at 8% of sales in base and 10% in bull; depreciation is not assumed to be maintenance capex.

Operating working capital rises ₹31.04→₹45.58 crore from FY25 to FY26, a ₹14.54 crore investment, and operating IC including deposits/PPE rises ₹44.81→₹64.35 crore. The book incremental return proxy 19.51% does not distinguish new investment returns from old-asset utilization, depreciation changes or inventory accounting. CAP stays NS, preventing a GQS point. The meaningful test is cash per share after funding inventory, customer credit, tooling and new products. Forecast paths retain operating cash, pay existing obligations and do not assume free refinancing. [S3][S4][S6][S13]

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text:
Promoter ownership is 71.83% in March 2026 versus 71.45% a year earlier; issued shares remain 16,094,060 in the October master. No ordinary new shares were issued in FY25–FY26. Current encumbrance, lock-in expiry and fully executable float are not established from a current shareholding filing. The predecessor business was transferred through noncash consideration before the IPO; the large bonus/share-count changes must not be confused with all-cash equity inflows or new operating value.

DGMS resigned in December 2024 citing preoccupation elsewhere. Its annexure says no other material reason; this explanation is preserved and the resignation is not described as a scope dispute. Kailash Chand Jain & Co. issued an unmodified FY26 opinion and internal-controls opinion. CARO reports no repayment default, no fraud identified and no disputed statutory dues, while noting slight delays in some undisputed payments. Those are positive but not conclusive assurance. Reporting inconsistencies in the notes still require reconciliation. Promoter-related remuneration ₹2.22 crore, rent ₹0.6720 crore, deposit ₹0.23 crore and sales to Exotic Planter ₹1.2851 crore are disclosed; management represents RPTs as ordinary-course/arm's-length. The rent total does not match the smaller expense-note rent and is an open query, not proof of diversion.

Promises versus delivery: shade-net expansion discussed 11 November 2024 is described as operating in the 2025 presentation, but product-level revenue and returns are ND. September 2025 trademark assignment at nil consideration is a concrete minority-alignment positive, with registry completion not authenticated. February 2026 airport orders total ₹0.8145 crore tax-inclusive with 30-day/six-month timelines; April Lucknow order ₹0.5074 crore had 90 days; collections/completion are not independently established. Fountains launched 19 April 2026, but incremental revenue is not disclosed. FY26 AGM voting-document retrieval was blocked: no final remuneration approval or dividend approval is inferred solely from an index/summary. [S1][S4][S6–S14]

sections.title: Financial Forensics
sections.text:
FY26 operating EBIT is ₹16.3394 crore and EBITDA ₹19.7431 crore after removing ₹0.0356 crore other income; reported PAT ₹12.5213 crore and diluted EPS ₹7.78 compare with ₹9.7008 crore/₹6.03 in FY25. A normalization sensitivity removes other income, adds old preliminary-expense amortization ₹0.4974 crore and taxes at 25%; FY25 also adds the disclosed ₹1.428 crore excess depreciation from a retrospective policy correction. These are analyst proxies, not corrected audited accounts. FY25's low effective tax rate and depreciation change complicate clean per-share earnings comparisons. Gross profit is ND because the materials/finished-goods bridge excludes conversion costs; no aggregator operating-profit line is relabeled gross profit.

FY26 cash bridge is ₹20.5616 crore pre-working-capital cash, plus employee-advance release ₹0.0088, less stock ₹14.6505, receivables ₹7.0335 and other CA ₹0.1799, plus current-liability/provision ₹4.8516 and supplier-credit ₹2.6670, less tax ₹2.6507, giving CFO ₹3.5744 crore within source rounding. Capex ₹8.5127 crore is investing cash, explaining FCF−₹4.9383 crore, not weak CFO. FY25–26 cumulative CFO ₹9.3414 divided by PAT ₹22.2221 is 42.04%, not an average of annual ratios. A debt-classification/financing-interest sensitivity gives 38.85%. The reported FY24–26 ratio is −19.30%, but FY24's noncash predecessor-opening-balance distortions make it unsuitable as the main conversion judgment.

Stock ₹38.2112 crore grew 62.18%, with finished goods ₹36.8184 crore or 96.35%; receivables ₹19.9432 crore grew 51.55%. Average receivable days worsen 78.42→87.93. Materials-consumption inventory-days proxies rise 155.65→218.32, not exact full-COGS days. Gross receivables over one year total ₹0.1963 crore and provision ₹0.25 crore; no large overdue balance is invented. Customer advances ₹6.537 crore versus ₹2.3786 supplied cash, an important counterpoint that also creates delivery obligations.

Debt is ₹4.2941 crore including ₹0.4392 current maturities, not merely ₹3.8549. Reported cash ₹0.9666 is not certified unrestricted October liquidity. Historical net debt/EBITDA 0.17× and EBIT/finance 49.27× look strong but are stale stock/flow comparisons. Operating IC reconciles to financing IC within ₹0.0003 crore rounding; ROIC proxy 22.45%, ROCE 29.94% and ROE 23.33% are not CAP scores. FY25 comparative assets/liabilities changed ₹1.4212 crore; reserves use a PBT-looking addition; FY26 debt movement, PPE cash/additions, property-title and rent notes need clarification. The full reconciliation register preserves each source and the company's depreciation/presentation explanations. [S1–S5]

sections.title: Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text:
At the stale ₹96 reference, market cap is ₹154.503 crore, reported P/E 12.34× and P/B 2.58×. Adding March debt and deducting reported cash gives historical EV ₹157.8305 crore, or 7.99× EBITDA. Current unrestricted cash is unverified, so this is not current October EV. No separate property, IPO cash, prepaid expense, warrant or hypothetical subsidiary value is added. Rent remains an operating expense; no undisclosed financing lease is invented.

Annual bear/base/bull models cover FY27 before/after entry, full FY28–FY31 and a 202/366 FY32 stub ending 19 October 2031. Base uses 15% annual growth,22.5% EBIT margin,67% ONWC/sales,8% capex/sales and 10× terminal EBIT. Bear links initial 10% sales loss,15% margin,80% ONWC,9% capex and a cash credit call with 7× terminal EBIT. Bull uses 25/25/22/20/18/16% fiscal growth,24% margin,60% ONWC,10% capex and 13× terminal EBIT. All pay normalized cash taxes,9.5% modeled interest, amortize term debt, retain 1% sales operating cash and reserve legacy tax ₹1.9205 crore once. A ₹0.25/share proposed dividend is reserved once before entry as a conservative assumption because the underlying final approval/payment is unverified; the October buyer receives none.

Actual current funding is unverified, so every ordinary IRR and ordinary entry price is null. Base and bear breach required cash before entry by ₹0.7884 crore and ₹4.1986 crore respectively; their non-rescue conditional IRRs/entry prices also remain null even though later hypothetical profits restore cash. Bull clears the assumed floor, producing a conditional 33.01% IRR and ₹198.71 hurdle-equivalent price, but only with aggressive growth, margin and working-capital improvement. This is not an ordinary target or validated entry range.

A separate rescue model issues integral shares at ₹67.20,30% below the reference, and charges 5% fees. Base requires 123,499 new shares and gives counterfactual 18.06% IRR/₹109.49 hurdle price; bear requires 678,843 shares and gives −11.56%/₹25.83. No financing is presumed available or approved. Fee/discount sensitivities and full annual cash/share ledgers are embedded. The 36-cell DCF tests 13–18% WACC,3–5% terminal growth and 12–22% terminal ROIC, funds terminal growth and cash floor growth, and uses signed entry cash minus floor, including the −₹0.7884 crore deficit without truncation. Base DCF outputs remain diagnostic, not investable prices. Growth/multiple and funding sensitivities retain feasibility flags. Reverse arithmetic at 10× terminal EBIT/22.5% margin needs about 13.33% annual revenue growth from modeled entry runrate before excess cash; it does not solve financing. [S4][M1][M2]

Equity-hurdle sensitivity at 12%, 15% and 18% is separate from the DCF cost of capital. Funding holds remain binding at every hurdle. The DCF terminal value contributes 77.05% to 88.76% of enterprise value across the tested grid, making long-run reinvestment, returns and discount-rate assumptions especially important. These are arithmetic diagnostics, not verified investment values.

sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text:
The central failure variable is inventory monetization at sufficient margin and collection speed. Revenue growth can appear healthy while expanding finished-goods stocks, receivables and tooling consume cash. If demand or product appeal weakens, stock may require markdowns; a simultaneous customer-payment slowdown and reduced advance orders can force borrowing or equity issuance even when the preceding balance sheet showed low net debt. A smaller terminal multiple then compounds operating disappointment into per-share loss.

The strongest counterargument to pessimism is real sales/PAT growth, positive FY25/FY26 CFO, relatively low debt, disclosed customer advances and a clean audit/no-default report. The strong bearish case must nevertheless address the magnitude of assets that must turn to cash: ₹38.21 crore inventory and ₹19.94 crore net receivables versus ₹0.97 crore reported cash. The embedded bear ties an initial 10% sales fall to 15% EBIT margin,80% ONWC/sales, sustained reinvestment and repayment of cash credit. Its first cash floor gap is ₹4.20 crore, so an ordinary return is withheld; even separate rescue at discount/fees produces a five-year loss. Those are stresses, not allegations of actual default.

Financial-note inconsistencies independently create a reliability hold. They could include presentation/reclassification errors, rented-premises improvements or accrual timing rather than intentional misstatement, but the explanation must reconcile amounts. A corrected report and satisfactory lender/cash evidence could clear the holds; a cheap price alone cannot. Inventory aging/realizability, customer advances and the capex/funding bridge are more informative than a single missed half-year. Confirmed diversion, a material unexplained write-off, default or inability to fund essential operations would be a thesis break, not normal volatility. [S1–S5]

sections.title: 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text:
A fivefold share-price outcome over five years requires 37.97% annualized appreciation; tenfold requires 58.49%, before any dividends. These are required rates, not forecasts. With unchanged attributable net margin, valuation multiple and share count, business revenue would need to reach approximately ₹343.55 crore for 5× or ₹687.09 crore for 10× from FY26 ₹68.709 crore. Constant definitions matter: predecessor sole-proprietor capital and pre-IPO bonus shares cannot be used as if they were an equivalent listed-share base.

The bull scenario reaches about ₹201.84 crore terminal TTMrevenue, still far below those simplistic 5×/10× revenue equivalents, and already requires sustained high growth,24% EBIT margin, improved working capital intensity and ongoing capex. Achieving more through multiple expansion is not intrinsic business compounding; dilution can erase part of enterprise growth. A lower terminal multiple, higher cash investment or stock markdown reduces per-share value markedly. A broad horticulture TAM or an airport customer does not establish access to the required sales.

The feasibility classification is Speculative / unsupported. The records do not support precise success probabilities, verified high incremental returns, proven unit capacity or a funded path to that scale. New evidence on channel unit economics, product realizations, independently reconciled capacity, conversion of expansion capital and stable collection behavior would be necessary before elevating the outcome. The separate sensitivity models quantify assumptions without turning speculative upside into a target. [S1][S4][S6][S13]

sections.title: Monitoring Plan
sections.text:
The monitoring table below is a research checklist, not a scheduled service or trading rule. First, obtain the next comparable half-year results and distinguish true volume/channel gains from price/mix. FY26 revenue ₹68.709 crore and H2 growth 14.67% are baselines; another slowing half-year deserves review, not automatic rejection. Second, inspect finished-goods and receivable cash release: inventory ₹38.2112 crore,96.35% finished goods, and receivable days 87.93 are baselines. A further material stock build without proportional sales/collections is an alert; inability to sell stock without material loss is a thesis break.

Third, reconcile CFO with bank movements and debt: two-year reported conversion 42.04% and debt ₹4.2941 crore are baselines. Sustained conversion toward 80% would improve evidence; continued sub- 50% conversion while capex continues needs a funded explanation. Fourth, require an issuer/auditor bridge for revised comparatives, reserves and current debt maturities; lack of an explanation sustains G2 rather than proving abuse. Fifth, verify current cash, restrictions, sanctioned/unused facilities and contractual repayment dates before allowing ordinary returns.

Sixth, compare shade-net/fountain sales, utilization and incremental returns with announcements and close the 210,000/350,000 kg capacity discrepancy. Seventh, verify fulfillment/collection of the tax-inclusive airport orders without treating orders as revenue. Eighth, review RPT rent/remuneration and actual AGM approvals, including trademark registry completion. Ninth, acquire official BSE 20/60-session turnover, quote date, lot and actual bid–ask depth for the proposed position; ₹432,000 in three full lots remains only an illustration. Thresholds are economic warning conditions, not statistically validated universal cutoffs. [S3–S14][M1][M2]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text:
Hold — unresolved. Research priority is resolving accounting/funding and execution evidence, not selecting a price target. The business has demonstrated meaningful nominal revenue expansion and plausible product extensions, but no evidence-backed compounder designation is supported: MOAT 4, GOV 5, CASH 4 and CAP NS fail the required thresholds even before critical holds. BQS and Growth Quality are incomplete, not low point estimates, and IAS is also NS because both return/funding and executable liquidity are unresolved.

The price-sensitive part is explicitly conditional on a stale ₹96 reference and a ₹5 lakh nominal budget. The actual floor position is three 1,500-share lots/₹432,000; it cannot be implemented as arbitrary fractional lots. Recent secondary observations imply no full-lot capacity at 5% participation across all 19 retrieved recent sessions. That is an execution warning, not a confirmed zero-trading or suspension finding. A verified current quote and live orderbook are required before any implementation decision.

Improved records could change the classification: reconciled reserves/comparatives, a complete cash/debt movement bridge, realistic inventory realization, current unused facilities and attributable expansion returns. A lower price may improve conditional return arithmetic, but cannot cure unreliable financial inputs, unavailable funding or unavailable liquidity. Existing holders would need their actual position, tax context and available exit liquidity considered separately; the research supplies no automatic buy/sell instruction. No trade is executed or authorized by this analysis. [S3–S5][M1][M2]

sections.title: Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text:
The source register retains exact underlying URLs, document dates where verified, original-byte SHA-256 digests, locators and authentication limits. Material financial claims use issuer annual reports, the official prospectus and underlying dated filings; the historical quote/volume series is explicitly secondary. The official interoperable security master verifies identity/share count/lot but is not a BSE bhavcopy or depth feed. Undated peer pages serve only as competition/product context. The inaccessible AGM voting PDF is a pointer, not evidence that a particular resolution passed. The issuer's unmodified audit, no-default statements, resignation explanation, depreciation correction and presentation-only materials reclassification are preserved alongside concerns.

Forecast growth, margins, capital intensity, taxes, rates, cash floor, terminal multiples and rescue terms are analyst assumptions. They are not management guidance or promised funding. Available cash is an upper-bound scenario assumption using reported March cash because restrictions/current balances are unverified. Legacy tax and the conservative pre-entry dividend reserve are paid only once; no IPO/property/prepaid/warrant add-on is used. Signed entry cash minus required operating cash is used even when negative. DCF terminal growth requires reinvestment at an explicit terminal ROIC and additional operating cash.

Open questions are concrete: why FY25 comparative assets/liabilities changed; why reserves use a PBT-looking addition; how FY26 debt maturities map to financing cashflow; whether factory structures are leasehold improvements; how RPT rent maps to expenses; what stock aging/product margins show; whether current facilities cover expansion/stress; which capacity figures are comparable; and what liquidity exists for whole lots. Original PDFs, HTML, extracted text/OCR, images and personal identifiers are excluded from analytical backups. Safe financial extracts, model code/results and URLs/hashes support reproducibility, not independent authentication of omitted sources. This is analytical research, not personalized investment advice or a trade instruction. [S1–S14][M1][M2][P1–P4]
